# pmon_users (Data Source)

Every locally known principal and the groups it belongs to.

Group membership is only visible from this side: a group listing reports how many members it has, never which.

**This writes every principal and email address into Terraform state.** Treat the state file accordingly, and prefer `pmon_groups` when you only need entitlements.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Writes every principal and email into state. Prefer pmon_groups when entitlements are enough.
data "pmon_users" "all" {}

output "admins" {
  value = [
    for u in data.pmon_users.all.users :
    u.principal if contains(u.group_names, "system:admin")
  ]
}

output "deactivated" {
  value = [for u in data.pmon_users.all.users : u.principal if !u.active]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `users` (Attributes List) The users, as pmon reports them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--users))

<a id="nestedatt--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `users`

Read-Only:

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the principal may authenticate. A deprovisioned user stays listed with this false.
- `created_at` (String) When pmon first saw the principal.
- `email` (String) Email address.
- `group_names` (List of String) Groups the principal belongs to, sorted.
- `id` (Number) pmon's internal id.
- `principal` (String) Principal as pmon knows it, usually an email address.
- `source` (String) `OIDC` for a principal provisioned at login, `LOCAL` otherwise.
